method: Resolve each suspected defect from the nearest controlling formula, definition, or explicit type.
Require an adjacent localized disclosure and an exact machine-readable delta for every translated repair.

findings.finding: The explanation correctly says r<=s iff s-r is nonnegative and the displayed definition computes [c,d]-[a,b], but the intervening phrase reverses that difference to r-s.
findings.controlling_evidence: Both the preceding clause and the immediately following display require s-r.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use s-r in both explanatory clauses and add an adjacent OLTEARITH-001 note.

findings.finding: A literal less-than character appears immediately after the plural element token and has no syntactic or mathematical role.
findings.controlling_evidence: The clause is ordinary prose saying all elements are smaller than 3.
findings.required_translation_handling: Omit only the stray character and add an adjacent OLTEARITH-002 note.

findings.finding: The nonnegative multiplication case unions with 0 superscript R, inconsistent with the p_Real embedding defined four lines earlier and with later 0_Real uses.
findings.controlling_evidence: The intended set is the embedded rational zero cut, denoted 0_Real throughout the surrounding construction.
findings.required_translation_handling: Replace 0 superscript mathbb R by 0_Real and add an adjacent OLTEARITH-003 note.

findings.finding: The proof says existence of a cut in S follows from S having an upper bound; it follows from the explicitly assumed non-emptiness of S.
findings.controlling_evidence: The theorem hypothesis says S is non-empty and bounded above; only the first hypothesis supplies a member.
findings.required_translation_handling: Attribute existence to non-emptiness and add an adjacent OLTEARITH-004 note.

findings.finding: The prose says real numbers are identified with equivalence relations, but the construction and next sentence identify them with equivalence classes under Realequiv.
findings.controlling_evidence: Lines 123-125 explicitly define reals as equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use equivalence classes and add an adjacent OLTEARITH-005 note.

findings.finding: The equivalence class representing a constructed real is compared with 0_Rat instead of the already defined embedded zero 0_Real.
findings.controlling_evidence: Lines 136-138 define q_Real as the real represented by the constant rational sequence c_q.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use 0_Real and add an adjacent OLTEARITH-006 note.

findings.finding: The theorem and exercise say Cauchy sequences constitute an ordered field, although equality and operations were defined on Realequiv equivalence classes.
findings.controlling_evidence: Lines 123-147 define the real objects and arithmetic on equivalence classes, not on raw sequences under literal equality.
findings.required_translation_handling: State the theorem and exercise for equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences and add an adjacent OLTEARITH-007 note.

findings.finding: The completeness statement calls S a set of sequences, then compares q_Real directly with r in S, while all later comparisons correctly use equivalence classes [h].
findings.controlling_evidence: The proof formulas from line 201 onward uniformly order equivalence classes equivrep(h); the one direct q_Real<r comparison is ill-typed.
findings.required_translation_handling: Describe S as representative sequences for a family of classes, compare q_Real with equivrep(r), and add an adjacent OLTEARITH-008 note.
